# Mean-only scalar localization loses the simplex-chain constraint

This is an exact obstruction to ONE proposed functional relaxation. It is
not a mixed-integer counterexample: the scalar law below is not a positive
normalized linear projection of uniform area on the standard triangle.

For the half-integer symmetric triangle chain put

    r_h=1-h/10, h=0,...,9,
    K_{-h}=K_{h+1}=r_h T_2,
    t=1/3, beta=1/60.

The radius sequence is positive and concave on the full integer support
-9,...,10: successive slopes are1/10 on the left,0 across the central
pair, and-1/10 on the right. Thus the lifted hull is an actual convex
body with precisely these original fibers.

A positive normalized continuous normal would induce the law Y=w.X,
X uniform T_2,w_i>=0,w1+w2=1. Such a law has mean1/3 and is a
1/2-concave probability measure. Consider the relaxation allowing ANY
1/2-concave law supported in[0,1] with that same mean. The half-integer
cap functional then becomes

    sum_{h=0}^9 r_h^2[
       P(r_h Y>=t-beta h)+P(r_h Y>=t+beta(h+1))].    (1)

This relaxation does not obey the desired lower bound
(4/9)sum r_h^2, even for a nonatomic log-concave law.

Indeed take Y uniform on

    [1/3-1/600, 1/3+1/600].

It is supported in[0,1], has mean1/3, and its density is a positive
constant on its convex support, so its density's first root is concave;
equivalently it is1/2-concave as required by this relaxation.
For every h>=1 the gap between the left threshold and r_h/3 is

    (1/3-h/60)-(1-h/10)/3=h/60>=1/60.

The possible upward deviation r_h/600 is at most1/600<1/60.
Thus every left outer tail in(1) is zero. Every right threshold exceeds
r_h/3 by at least beta=1/60, so every right tail is likewise zero.
At the sole left central term h=0, the threshold is exactly the mean,
and the nonatomic uniform law contributes1/2. Therefore(1) is exactly

    1/2,

whereas

    sum_{h=0}^9 r_h^2=(1^2+...+10^2)/100=77/20,
    (4/9)sum r_h^2=77/45>1/2.                      (2)

All inequalities are strict away from the own central cut; no issue
with open versus closed boundary mass is present.

The law is provably not a valid normalized triangle projection. For
X uniform T_2 and w1+w2=1,

    Var(w.X)=[3(w1^2+w2^2)-1]/36>=1/72,

using w1^2+w2^2>=1/2. The chosen uniform law has variance
(1/300)^2/12=1/1080000, strictly smaller. Also every genuine positive
projection has zero in its support, whereas this relaxed law does not.

Thus retaining only the mean, nonnegative support inside[0,1], and the
usual concavity class is insufficient for a chain-wide localization
argument. The exact Dirichlet or radial-angular structure, or another
additional quantitative constraint excluding this relaxation, must remain.
This observation does not contradict any original cap inequality.
